thread:
clare: Observed another perf regression on the 8xA100 TPU-like rig during long sequences. Latency spikes ~300ms every few minutes, looks like short network microbursts triggering all-reduce backpressure and KV cache churn.

diego: Can you paste the perf summary? microbursts sound like NIC buffer saturation or unexpected flushes.

clare: Pasted top summary from profiler:

```
TIMELINE SUMMARY (20s window):
compute: 54.2% (steady)
allreduce: 27.9% (bursty waits)
kv-cache-ops: 8.1% (evict/refresh spikes)
ipc-wait: 6.5% (net microbursts)
other: 3.3%
```

clare: Also saw these in the kernel selector logs: frequent fallback to small-token kernels with `fragmented=true` flagged.

sam: That kernel fallback + small batches = lots of tiny allreduces. If NVLink is shared with other tenants, microbursts could push overruns to PCIe/EFA path.

li: On the EFA nodes we saw retransmits around the same times. If a single rank temporarily saturates its NVLink peers, ring algorithms fall back to PCIe or EFA and latency explodes.

perf-bot: Automated test 'ci/rt/multi-gpu/kv-shard-longseq' failed with >2x tail latency; regression introduced between commit abc123 and def456. Suspect batching heuristics change.

diego: Quick hypothesis list: 1) batching heuristic now slices too fine for long sequences; 2) KV cache eviction is thrashing because prefetch window misestimated; 3) kernel selector prefers low-latency kernel that defeats comm/compute overlap.

clare: I dumped a short perf trace with timestamps and a condensed net log:

```
[00:12:02.345] rank0 finish compute
[00:12:02.356] rank0 start allreduce
[00:12:02.360] NVLINK util spike -> 90%
[00:12:02.370] rank2 delayed (PCIe fallback)
[00:12:02.381] allreduce stalls 120ms
[00:12:05.004] kv-cache evict burst (3k entries)
```

sam: That 120ms stall lines up with our retransmit window on EFA. Do we have commit that changed `batch_slicing_threshold`?

perf-bot: Changeset summary: def456 adjusted `max_batch_tokens` to optimize memory; introduced adaptive slice when `seq_len>1024`.

li: Adaptive slicing might create smaller per-rank chunks asymmetrically. That breaks our allreduce aggregation plan (we expect uniform chunk sizes for ringlet scheduling).

clare: Reproducer plan: 1) run long-seq workload with `max_batch_tokens` pinned to old value; 2) run with NVLink-only topology (disable EFA overlay) and compare; 3) enable verbose kernel selection tracing.

diego: For (2) do on the dedicated pool that has NVLink fully connected, and also on a mixed-host rack to stress PCIe/EFA. If difference is large, routing fallback is the culprit.

sam: Short-term mitigation: bump `min_slice_tokens` so we don't produce <128-token fragments, and force kernel selector to prefer the larger-kernel path when seq_len>2048. That should reduce allreduce chatter.

li: Also add a KV prefetch cooldown so we don't evict aggressively after a small prefix miss burst. Put it behind an opt-in flag for now.

clare: I'll run the pinned experiments and post traces. If we confirm, I'll open a rollback PR for the adaptive-slice and a targeted fix for kernel heuristics.

perf-bot: CI job queued: `perf/regressions/2154321000-repro`.

infra-bot: Noted: scheduling NVLink-only runs may take 2h due to capacity. Putting them at top of queue.

clare: Thx. If anyone has quick ideas on faster mitigations (software-level) please ping. @diego @sam :thinking_face:

diego: I'll prototype forcing coalesced allreduces (aggregate small fragments into a single op before network dispatch). Could reduce interrupts.

sam: I can add additional metrics to the console: full per-rank NVLink/PCIe counters and per-allreduce payload sizes. That will make these spikes easier to correlate to kernel choices.

clare: Great. I'll upload the initial traces in ~45m. End for now. :thumbsup:
